target.title: feat(cli): add openclaw promos to discover and claim ClawHub promotional model offers
target.body:
Closes #100234

### What Problem This Solves

ClawHub publishes time-boxed promotional model offers (`GET /api/v1/promotions`), but existing OpenClaw users have no way to activate one short of re-running onboarding or hand-editing config. Offers expire on a schedule, so activation must be fast and must not require an OpenClaw release per promotion.

### Why This Change Was Made

Adds an `openclaw promos` command group (`list`, `claim <slug>`) that turns a claim into a ~30-second flow while treating the remote payload as strictly declarative:

- Every remote identifier is contract-validated at the parse boundary (`src/infra/clawhub.ts`): slug (`[a-z0-9-]`), model refs (shell-safe, must start with the promotion's declared provider), provider/authChoiceId/pluginNames (identifier grammar). Display text is `sanitizeTerminalText`-ed at output. A malformed or compromised promotion cannot make the CLI execute anything, print terminal controls, or emit unsafe copy-paste commands.
- Auth reuses existing machinery end-to-end: unknown auth-choice ids are refused with an "update OpenClaw" message (manifest choices first, install catalog second — mirroring `applyAuthChoiceLoadedPluginProvider`); existing provider credentials are reused only when the provider plugin is actually installed; otherwise the provider's normal auth-choice flow runs (install + enable + auth), with completion revalidated before any config write. `--api-key` follows the shipped `onboard --<provider>-api-key`/`--token` non-interactive contract; provider env vars work with no flag at all.
- Models register through the canonical config mutators (`upsertCanonicalModelConfigEntry`); aliases are held to the `models aliases add` contract and never overwrite existing aliases; plugin enablement is enforced (policy-blocked plugins refuse the claim); setting the suggested default is offered — never forced — and runs the same Codex/Copilot runtime-plugin repair as `openclaw models set`.
- Zero new config keys, env vars, or state files.

### User Impact

Existing users can run `openclaw promos list`, then `openclaw promos claim <slug>` (optionally `--api-key`/`--set-default` for non-interactive use) and immediately use promotional models. Nothing about their defaults, aliases, or credentials changes without explicit consent. New docs page: `docs/cli/promos.md`.

### Evidence

- Unit tests: 29 across `src/commands/promos/claim.test.ts` (13), `list.test.ts` (4), `src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` (9), covering payload validation (shell metacharacters, inverted windows, foreign-provider models/auth choices), auth completeness (retrySelection, post-apply revalidation, plugin policy refusal, install-catalog vs manifest provenance), alias contract, default + runtime repair, and 404/ended handling. `pnpm test src/commands/promos src/infra/clawhub.promotions.test.ts` green.
- Gates: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, scoped `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `oxfmt`, `pnpm docs:check-links`, `pnpm docs:map:check`, full `pnpm build` (no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`).
- Live end-to-end against a local ClawHub instance in an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`: `promos list` renders the offer; `promos claim <slug> --api-key … --set-default` installs nothing extra for the bundled provider, stores the credential in the agent auth-profile store, registers the model + alias, sets the default; rejection paths verified live (unknown auth choice → "update OpenClaw", unknown slug → friendly 404 message).
- Structured review (Codex/gpt-5.5) run to a clean final pass; earlier passes' findings (auth completeness, terminal sanitization, window trust, slug/model-ref/identifier contracts, plugin install/enable enforcement, runtime repair) are each fixed with regression tests. Two reviewer suggestions were consciously rejected with sibling-contract evidence, documented inline: argv `--api-key` (matches shipped onboard non-interactive flags) and provider-credential reuse (deliberate contract; now gated by install provenance and plugin policy).
